## 50% BMP with DOPE-Biotin and DOPE-Cy5

I prepared two SLB samples. In both sample I can see the membrane (not its
fluidity) in the confocal image (DOPE-Cy5 channel). However, When I switch to
iSCAT acquisition, I can only see stationary GNPs (not undergoing Brownian
motion). I tried different regions of the sample, but I couldn't find any mobile
GNPs. Therefore, I prepared a new batch of SUV for 25% BMP with DOPE-Biotin and
DOPE-Cy5 markers which has a better chance of success when preparing the SLB
sample.

## Single Molecule Emitter Validation (Single Step Fitting)


The histogram shows
a unimodal distribution, it is likely that the signal is from a single molecule.
In the figure above, the histogram show single-emitter step size (ΔI) 306±158.
a.u. Here, I filtered more than 7000 trajectories and found 167 trajectories
that shows clear signal drops. I have tested this on sample with TAT-B with 25%
BMP. Please note that
the analysis was done on the sum of all pixels designated to
a particle that trackpy reports. 

| Metric | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Total trajectories in dataset | 7,747 |
| Trajectories $\ge$ 15 frames analyzed | 7,747 |
| Qualifying single-step bleach events | 163 (2.1% of analyzed) |
| Average single-molecule step size ($\Delta I$) | $306.98 \pm 158.53$ |
| Average background noise level ($\sigma$) | $56.86 \pm 39.64$ |
| Average Step Signal-to-Noise Ratio | 7.06 |

## Single Molecule Emitter Validation (Histogram)

I also tried to plot the histogram of the signal intensity for all trajectories at 
different time points. The histogram shows a unimodal distribution, but they could be from multiple emitters. Therefore, I think the multistep fitting is a better way to validate the single molecule emitter.
